chapters.title: Use LP membership to remove redundant vertices
chapters.summary: The midpoint is a convex combination of opposite corners. Removing it leaves the unit square unchanged. Membership decisions use the registered numerical LP and specified bounded checks. Resource stops and incomplete outcomes must remain visible.
chapters.mathematical_input: V={(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1),(0.5,0.5)}. The reducer tests each row against the convex hull of the remaining rows.
chapters.expected_output: Installed hull client: canonical square and completed registered LP receipts passed

chapters.support_limits: The result uses numerical HiGHS LP receipts. The client checks completion and retained source indices. It does not certify exact arithmetic, and the client exercises three reducers only; the other inventory entries remain reference-only. chapters.title: Compare source-index hull methods in a 2D operation
chapters.summary: Check every input point, including interior points, edge points, and duplicates. KPABEP/MODIF preserve source order, pivots, epsilon, and stops. QuickHull is a distinct modern comparator. Saved timings do not imply a general speedup.
chapters.mathematical_input: The ordered cloud is [(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1),(0.5,0),(0,0),(1/3,1/3)]. The affine map is (x,y) ↦ (x+0.25, 0.5x+y−0.5). The one-step sum adds x0=(0.25,0.5) to the same control square. The BTULSHOR run also submits the cloud [(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1),(0.5,1.00000001)] under the identity affine map and retains its unsupported or stopped outcome. The separate installed legacy client uses MODIF A=[1,2,−1]ᵀ, x=[1,2,−1]ᵀ, initial status 1; KPABEP uses the square with center (0.5,0.5); REACH uses A=I, B=[1,2]ᵀ, initial vertices (0,0),(1,0) and control vertices 0,1.
chapters.expected_output: Both source-index runs return affine-image vertices {(0.25,-0.5),(1.25,0),(1.25,1),(0.25,0.5)} and one-step-sum vertices {(0.25,0.5),(1.25,0.5),(1.25,1.5),(0.25,1.5)}. Each reports checker status=verified. The legacy consumer reports MODIF, KPABEP port and REACH source pairs passed.
chapters.intermediate_geometry: The affine map produces vertical edges at x=0.25 and x=1.25. Its lower-left vertex is below y=0. Adding x0=(0.25,0.5) to the unit control square produces the translated square [0.25,1.25]×[0.5,1.5].
chapters.support_limits: The saved source-index result is a bounded 2D numerical operation with a 5,000 ms and 64-point exact checker. The checker verifies every generated input point is contained by the selected source IDs; it does not prove minimality. BTULSHOR preserves source-order behavior. These outputs are not a performance comparison or historical REACH reproduction. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter. Its CTest installs the current package and builds the isolated clients with find_package(CSL CONFIG).

chapters.title: Keep terminal optimization separate from membership
chapters.summary: A Strategy A linear terminal program returns the complete minimum-cost segment. A separate convex residual-norm terminal program returns one numerical minimizer. Neither result is a vertex membership decision.
chapters.mathematical_input: Linear terminal program: choose (x,y)∈[0,1]² with x+y≥1 and minimize x+y. Convex program: minimize ||[1,0]ᵀx−[3,−4]ᵀ|| for scalar 0≤x≤2; the adapter minimizes the squared norm. The nominal one-step model has state map A=0, control map B=I, initial state (0,0), affine offset (0,0), and control box [0,1]².
chapters.expected_output:
profile=strategy-a.nominal-linear-exact-v1
state_dimension=2 control_dimension=2 horizon=1
terminal_constraint=x+y>=1; 0<=x,y<=1
objective=minimize x+y
exact_optimum=1 optimal_face={(x,y): x+y=1, 0<=x,y<=1}
verified_complete_family=true assurance=numerical
backend=csl.convex.highs version=1.0.0+highs.1.11.0
x=2 original_cost=4.123105626 squared_cost=17
termination=completed outcome=optimal evidence=unestablished
No certified bounds or optimal-family result.
chapters.intermediate_geometry: The linear feasible set is the unit square clipped by x+y≥1. Its minimum-cost face is the segment from (1,0) to (0,1). The convex residual-norm problem has a scalar feasible interval [0,2] and selects its right endpoint z=2.
chapters.support_limits: The complete-family result applies only to the registered nominal linear exact profile and one stage. The convex adapter reports one numerical minimizer for its squared residual-norm program; it does not report certified bounds or an optimal family. Both terminal optimization roles remain distinct from vertex membership and redundancy removal. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter.

chapters.title: Compare five set representations on one square
chapters.summary: This analytic calculation compares H/V polytopes, zonotopes, parallelotopes, ellipsoids and boxes on one square. Its Python script does not invoke CSL APIs.
chapters.mathematical_input: Q=[-1,1]^2. H rows: ±x<=1, ±y<=1. V corners: (±1,±1). Z center 0, generators e1,e2. Parallelotope A[-1,1]^2 with A=I. E={x:xᵀx<=2}. All centers are zero, generator coefficients lie in [−1,1], and support is evaluated in directions (1,0) and (1,1).
chapters.expected_output:
d=(1.0, 0.0); exact_square=1; outer_disk=1.41421
d=(1.0, 1.0); exact_square=2; outer_disk=2
polytope=exact zonotope=exact parallelotope=exact ellipsoid=outer box=exact
Q subset E; E subset [-sqrt(2),sqrt(2)]^2; Q is [-1,1]^2
chapters.intermediate_geometry: At d=(1,0), Q support is 1 and the enclosing disk support is √2. At d=(1,1), both supports equal 2. Q⊂E⊂[-√2,√2]².
chapters.support_limits: The square, zonotope, parallelotope, and box describe the same exact set in this example. The disk is an outer enclosure. No CSL API is called by this script.

chapters.title: Run the installed set approximation consumers
chapters.summary: Installed clients execute the public box, parallelotope, zonotope-reduction, and ellipsoid APIs on declared inputs. The box and parallelotope clients use the same diamond; the two other clients use their own specified sets.
chapters.mathematical_input: The box/parallelotope client encloses a four-vertex diamond. The zonotope client reduces center 0 with generators e1, e2, and (0.5,0.5). The ellipsoidal client checks two outer members for a square. The diamond clients request four H rows and use the axis or displayed fixed direction matrix. The zonotope requests two generators with independent coefficients in [−1,1] and no factor constraints. Each directional ellipsoid member requests one outer ellipsoid; the family is their intersection. All vertex inputs have no rays.
chapters.expected_output:
Installed box approximation client: diamond is enclosed with bounds 2 on both axes
Installed box/parallelotope client: rotated diamond bounds passed
Installed zonotope client: independently admitted axis cover passed
Installed ellipsoidal client: two reviewed outer members passed
chapters.intermediate_geometry: Both the box and rotated parallelotope use the diamond with vertices (0,2),(2,0),(0,-2),(-2,0). The axis-aligned box is [-2,2]². The rotated parallelotope uses directions (1,1) and (1,-1) with bounds 2. The zonotope cover uses generators (1.5,0) and (0,1.5). The ellipsoid client checks two separately reviewed outer members.
chapters.support_limits: These are three separate numerical consumer examples, not interchangeable representations of one exact result. The zonotope output is an outer cover. The ellipsoid result is an outer family. Each result has the assurance stated by its client. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter. Its CTest installs the current package and builds the isolated clients with find_package(CSL CONFIG).

chapters.title: Read a closed-loop policy trace
chapters.summary: Separate predicted stage coordinates from observed execution state and label the observation update. A deterministic replay is one trajectory. It is not full forward reachability or a nonlinear enclosure.
chapters.mathematical_input: Discrete plant x[k+1]=x[k]+u[k]. At each of two updates, observe x[k], choose u[k]=1-x[k], predict one stage, apply the action, and observe the new state.
chapters.expected_output:
update=0 observation=0 action=1 prediction_end=1 plant_state=1
update=1 observation=1 action=0 prediction_end=1 plant_state=1
chapters.intermediate_geometry: At each update, the one-stage prediction endpoint matches the observed plant state. The trace is one policy-conditioned path in a scalar state coordinate.
chapters.support_limits: This dependency-free discrete example illustrates observation and action timing. It does not invoke a CSL controller or establish full reachability, feasibility for other states, or an enclosure.

chapters.summary: The complete optimal joint family is (x0,x1,x2,u0,u1)=(0,s,1,s,1-s), 0<=s<=1. The exact-family verifier applies only to its registered profiles. Generic Strategy A/B paths are numerical candidates. Local NLP MPC makes no global optimum claim.
chapters.mathematical_input: The discrete two-stage integrator is x1=x0+u0, x2=x1+u1 with x0=0, ui∈[0,1], and cost (x2−1)². The exact complete optimal family is (x0,x1,x2,u0,u1)=(0,s,1,s,1−s), 0≤s≤1.

build/dev/installed-consumer/examples-build/registered_synthesis_comparison examples/scenarios/two-stage-integrator.json | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print("schema="+d["schema"]); [print(r["strategy"]+" termination="+r["termination"]+" outcome="+r["outcome"]+" witnesses="+str(len(r["witnesses"]))+" objective="+str(r["witnesses"][0]["recomputed_objective"])) for r in d["results"]]'

chapters.title: Convert, map, sum, intersect, and project sets
chapters.group_label: 4. Conversions, set operations, approximations and optimization
chapters.summary: Four installed consumers convert the unit square, sum unit intervals, intersect scalar half-spaces, and compute a nominal predecessor. The results are the unit square, [0,2], [0,1], and [1,3], respectively.
chapters.mathematical_input: Convert the unit square between H and V forms. Compute [0,1]+[0,1]. Intersect x≤1 with −x≤0. Compute the nominal predecessor {x : ∃u∈[−1,1], x+u=2}.
chapters.expected_output:
Installed Qhull conversion client: H-to-V square vertices passed
Installed Qhull conversion client: V-to-H square inequalities passed
Installed affine/sum client: selected LP and hull providers produced a numerical set result
Installed polyhedral client: public H intersection passed
Installed predecessor client: existential integrator interval and unestablished support passed
chapters.intermediate_geometry: H-to-V returns the four unit-square corners. V-to-H returns the four unit-square bounds. The interval sum is [0,2]. The H intersection is [0,1] with two rows. The existential predecessor is [1,3]; the consumer accepts 1 and 3 but rejects 0.875 and 3.125.
chapters.support_limits: Qhull conversion and affine sums use numerical providers and bounded client inputs. The predecessor has unestablished support assurance. The projection demonstrates an existential predecessor for one scalar integrator, not a general full-state intersection. Projected overlap does not prove full-state intersection. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter. Its CTest installs the current package and builds the isolated clients with find_package(CSL CONFIG).

chapters.mathematical_conclusion: The four installed clients return: H-to-V and V-to-H conversion of [0,1]²; the Minkowski sum [0,1]+[0,1]=[0,2]; the H intersection [0,1]; and the nominal predecessor {x : ∃u∈[−1,1], x+u=2}=[1,3].
